cells.tense: Something half-seen has your attention, and you are letting it lead you forward.
cells.ask: Take one small step today toward the direction that has felt most alive lately — make the call, write the note — before you know how it turns out.
cells.core:
There is enough light for the next step and no more, and you let that be enough. You move without demanding the whole road first, and the direction tends to get clearer after you act rather than before.

That is the skill of this place, and it is running clean. Most people need the outcome settled before they move. You can move while it stays open, and the moving is what shows you where you are going. Keep the pen in your hand by going on what you can see and letting the rest stay half-seen a while longer. Nothing here needs to be forced shut to be travelled.

cells.verb: Moving toward one direction as the pull becomes clear enough to follow

cells.tense: You are bracing for a decision that has not been made yet, arranging today around it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are arranging your days around that hasn't happened, and leave it unarranged for one day.
cells.core:
The future gets built in advance, and each choice bends toward it as if it were already settled. Nothing stays open long enough to be met on its own terms.

When you build the outcome before it arrives, the pull stops being a pull and becomes a position to defend. The step that was right in front of you disappears behind the one you have already taken in your head. The smaller move is closer than the bracing: find one thing you are trying to secure ahead of time and let it sit unresolved for a day. Not dropped. Just not decided. Direction can come from what is actually here rather than from what you have planned, and the care that does that does not exhaust.

cells.tense: You felt a pull toward something, and following it is not where you are now.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you are unsure about, and let their answer land without arguing with it or treating it as instructions.
cells.core:
The attention is still there, and your days are built around not walking into it. This is not patience. It is a quiet patch where the pull used to be.

What is missing is not effort — that has been spent. It is the plain sense of which direction is real, the kind that lands without needing an argument. That sense is still alive in another form: comfort with not knowing the whole road. Put one true thing in front of you today and let it count without justifying it to anyone, including yourself. Relief from the not-knowing comes through letting one small thing be true, not through pushing at the silence.

cells.tense: You are already moving toward a chosen direction and calling it something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Write down the direction you have already chosen, one reason it is yours, and keep the note where you will see it.
cells.core:
The choice shows in what you notice, what you say yes to, which half-open doors you walk through. But when you talk about it, it sounds like something that arrived on its own. The steering is real. The owning of it is not.

The simpler thing underneath is practice that does not force — time alone that connects rather than isolates, refinement that serves your growth rather than your worry. There is no need to decide again. Say that you already did. Put your name on it, out loud or on paper, so it stops feeling like it chose you and starts being the thing you chose.
